notes: Derived edit. The building-to-city rule is a SWRL rule (in_time_zone is functional, so it can't be the target of an OWL chain). Since 2026-10-31 the adds hold only the side facts the record's worlds name, not the answer (FINDINGS E): w1, the Needle stands in some other city with some time zone (placeholders); w2, Washington State and Seattle share one zone (a placeholder). Central Time then follows from the edit, the building rule and in_time_zone being functional.

queries.find: needle : located_in some (City and in_time_zone value ?)

fol.notes: Places and time zones are uninterpreted sorts; in_time_zone (RELATIONS.md, functional) is a function from a place to its zone, a belief the edit and the worlds can move. The building-to-city rule, Seattle being a city in Washington, the zones' UTC offsets (standard time) and the clock rule are firm, as in the DL file. The clock rule reads the Needle's local time off Chicago's through the two zones' offsets; Chicago observing Central Time is the stored bridge. Fact ids, gives_up and worlds are the DL file's. The adds are the worlds' side facts (w1: the Needle stands in some other city, a placeholder; w2: the state and Seattle share one zone), as in the DL file.

needle_seattle.says: The Space Needle is in Seattle.

wa_pacific.says: Washington State, Seattle included, observes Pacific Time.

building_rule.says: A building observes the time zone of the city it stands in.
building_rule.z3: ForAll([b, c], Implies(And(located_in(b, c), city(c)), in_time_zone(b) == in_time_zone(c)))

zones.says: Pacific Time is UTC−8 and Central Time UTC−6 (standard time); they are different zones.

clock_rule.says: At one moment, the clock time at a place is the time in Chicago shifted by the difference between the two places' UTC offsets.
